reports.title: TYSON FOODS REPORTS FOURTH QUARTER AND FISCAL 2026 RESULTS

guidance.heading: OUTLOOK
section: USDA projects domestic production will decrease approximately 2% in fiscal 2027 as compared to fiscal 2026. We anticipate segment operating income (loss), as adjusted, of $(300) million to $100 million in fiscal 2027.

desk.headline: Q4 sales up 5% to $14.6bn helped by an extra week, adjusted EPS $0.61 just above estimate; FY27 sales seen down 3.5–5.5%
results: Reported Q4 sales rose 5.2% to $14.6bn, but that includes a 14th week; on a like-for-like basis sales fell about 4%.
Adjusted EPS fell 47% to $0.61 (est. $0.60); a GAAP loss of $0.22 a share reflected $254m of restructuring charges and $124m of legal accruals.
Beef lost more money as cattle stayed scarce; chicken profit fell to $389m from $562m, while Prepared Foods grew profit to $321m.
For fiscal 2026, adjusted EPS fell 17% to $3.44 and adjusted operating income 14% to $1.98bn.
Free cash flow rose to $1.66bn; debt was cut by $1.08bn and 7.8m shares were bought back for $427m.

guidance.summary: First outlook for fiscal 2027: sales to fall 3.5–5.5% (vs 52-week FY26) on lower beef volumes, with adjusted operating income of $1.7–2.15bn against $1.98bn in FY26. The quarterly dividend rises 2% to $0.52.

points: Management called beef's losses a cattle-cycle problem; the network is being rebuilt around three main plants and the Pasco, Washington plant is for sale.
The CFO warned that market headwinds, mainly in chicken and pork, could outweigh cost savings in fiscal 2027.
Chicken volumes grew for an eighth straight quarter, but higher grain, feed and freight costs weighed on Q4 margins.
Prepared Foods gained market share; the CEO said innovation success is not yet where it needs to be.
Leverage is 2.1x net debt to adjusted EBITDA; a further $93m of shares were bought early in fiscal 2027.
call.source: Q4 2026 earnings call transcript — The Motley Fool, 16 Nov 2026; FY27 sales consensus from Reuters, 16 Nov 2026

watch: Beef margins and cattle supply, including Mexican cattle imports and the Amarillo second shift.
Chicken profit as grain and feed costs rise.
Progress on the Pasco plant sale and the effect on the beef outlook.
